stem: An avid runner taking ciprofloxacin develops new Achilles tendon pain and swelling after several doses. Which instruction is most appropriate?

options.A: Stop ciprofloxacin, contact the healthcare provider promptly, rest the affected tendon, and refrain from exercise until evaluated.
options.B: Continue ciprofloxacin while temporarily reducing running, and report the problem only if swelling or functional limitation worsens.
options.C: Continue ciprofloxacin and add a calcium supplement because calcium lowers the risk of fluoroquinolone tendon injury.
options.D: Finish the ciprofloxacin course before reporting tendon symptoms unless a tendon rupture occurs.

rationale: CIPRO carries a boxed warning for serious adverse reactions including tendinitis and tendon rupture. Current labeling directs immediate discontinuation if tendon pain, swelling, inflammation, or rupture occurs. Patient counseling specifically instructs patients with tendon pain or swelling to contact a healthcare provider, rest and refrain from exercise, and discontinue CIPRO. Continuing therapy, delaying reporting until rupture, or adding calcium is inconsistent with the label; calcium-containing products can also reduce ciprofloxacin absorption when taken concomitantly.
educational_objective: Respond to new tendon pain or swelling during ciprofloxacin therapy by stopping the drug, contacting the healthcare provider, and resting/refraining from exercise of the affected tendon.

source_claim_supported: Section 5.2 directs immediate discontinuation for tendon pain, swelling, inflammation, or rupture. Patient counseling directs contact with the provider, rest and refraining from exercise, and discontinuation. The interaction section states multivalent cation products decrease CIPRO absorption and require separation rather than being used to prevent tendon injury.

source_original.stem: An avid runner taking ciprofloxacin develops new Achilles tendon pain and swelling after several doses. Which instruction is most appropriate?

options.A: Stop ciprofloxacin and contact the prescriber promptly; avoid stressing the tendon until evaluated.
options.B: Continue ciprofloxacin while temporarily reducing running, and report the problem if swelling or functional limitation develops.
options.C: Take each dose with calcium to reduce the risk of tendon rupture.
options.D: Finish the course before reporting tendon symptoms unless a rupture occurs.

source_original.rationale: Fluoroquinolones, including ciprofloxacin, can cause tendinitis and tendon rupture, sometimes with disabling or irreversible adverse effects. New tendon pain or swelling during therapy warrants stopping the fluoroquinolone and prompt clinical review, with avoidance of exercise or loading of the affected tendon until evaluated.
source_original.source_detail: DailyMed CIPRO label — BOXED WARNING / Warnings and Precautions, Tendinitis and Tendon Rupture: discontinue with tendon pain/swelling and avoid stressing the affected tendon. correction_summary: Retained the stem and key. Reworded option A to mirror the label's explicit counseling language: discontinue, contact the provider, rest, and refrain from exercise. Rewrote option C so its error is clinically grounded: calcium does not prevent tendon injury and may reduce ciprofloxacin absorption if coadministered. Updated currentness metadata to the March 2, 2026 DailyMed update.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current brand CIPRO DailyMed prescribing information from Bayer.
audit_findings.currentness: Exact version 32 page reports Updated March 2, 2026; rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: §5.2 and §17 directly support immediate discontinuation, provider contact, rest, and refraining from exercise.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No unsupported tendon-risk threshold, duration, or exercise interval was introduced. The calcium distractor was checked against the label's multivalent-cation interaction.

distractor_audit.A: Directly supported by §5.2 and patient counseling; uniquely best.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because the label directs immediate discontinuation at tendon pain/swelling rather than continued therapy until worsening.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because calcium is not protective and concomitant multivalent cations can reduce CIPRO absorption.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because reporting and discontinuation should occur at tendon symptoms, before rupture.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A satisfies all labeled actions at the symptom stage described.
audit_findings.cueing: Options are all action-oriented medication instructions; the key requires recognizing the boxed-warning response.
audit_findings.blueprint: NCSBN 2026 Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies includes medication teaching and adverse-response evaluation.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Adversarial review confirmed that 'rest and refrain from exercise' is explicitly in patient counseling and that the item does not invent a duration for activity restriction.
